k_of_n.quote: One or more of the following physical functional impairments exists:

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Inline negatives: 'Orthognathic surgery when performed for cosmetic purposes does not meet the definition of medical necessity.' Genioplasty for appearance 'cosmetic and non-covered'. Dental items 'subject to coverage available through dental benefits'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: meets the definition of medical necessity when the (1.) skeletal deformity, (2.) functional impairment and (3.) documentation requirements below are met.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The 'and' is a list join of three numbered sections, i.e. ALL, but nothing says so with the capitalised AND the policy uses elsewhere.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Obstructive sleep apnea, when ALL of the following are met: Criteria for a positive airway pressure (PAP) device are met and the member is unable to tolerate PAP or has failed a trial of PAP
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Lower-case 'and' inside a bullet that is itself one of two ALL items: nested boolean in prose. Also delegates PAP criteria to another policy (09-E0000-21).

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Skeletal deformities, either A or B: A. One or more of the following skeletal deformities exists: ... B. There is a skeletal abnormality due to injury / trauma
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Alternatives are signalled by 'either A or B' in the lead-in, while within A the OR is repeated at the end of each bullet.

requirement_kinds.quote: Panorex and cephalometric radiographs; AND Cephalometric tracings and analysis
horizontal overjet of +5 millimeters (mm) or more
Masticatory (chewing) dysfunction due to skeletal deformity
Myofascial pain ... persisted for at least 6 months and has not responded to conservative therapy such as physical therapy or splinting
Photographs that demonstrate the skeletal deformity.
The member must have a confirmed diagnosis of cleft palate, with or without cleft lip, with a demonstrated malocclusion.
unable to tolerate PAP or has failed a trial of PAP

thresholds.quote: horizontal overjet of +5 millimeters (mm) or more, OR horizontal overjet of zero to a negative value (established norm = 2mm)
antero-posterior molar relationship discrepancy of 4mm or more (established norm = 0 to 1mm)
Unilateral or bilateral posterior open bite greater than 2mm

thresholds.quantity: palatal cusp to mandibular fossa discrepancy
thresholds.quote: Total bilateral maxillary palatal cusp to mandibular fossa discrepancy of 4mm or greater, or a unilateral discrepancy of 3mm or greater
asymmetry greater than 3mm with concomitant occlusal asymmetry

extraction_hazards: Mixed numbering styles in one list: '1.' / 'A.' / bullets / en-dashes ('−') for the 4th level; indentation is the only nesting signal in pdftotext.
Position Statement starts with a '*NOTE' that has its own '1.' list (statute text) that looks like criteria item 1 and collides with the real '1. Skeletal deformities'.
Description repeats the AAOMS A-D lettered list with different numbers than the Position Statement.
CPT table descriptions wrap onto 2-3 lines; the code is at column 0 only on the first line.
Cross-reference typo in the Position Statement ('Obstructive sleep apnea... 09-E0000-21') is fine, but RELATED GUIDELINES lists TMJ as '02/20000-12' with a slash instead of hyphen.
interesting_structures: Real three-part test with numeric dental/skeletal thresholds and a documentation checklist (radiographs, tracings, photos): the closest BCBSFL gets to InterQual-style criteria.
Statute-driven carve-outs (cleft lip/palate under 18; jaw parity) written into both the Position Statement and OTHER.
Dental vs medical boundary lists (torus surgery, endosteal implants, non-cleft orthodontics go to dental benefit).

fit_to_tree.why: Maps cleanly to all/any, but three problems: nesting is 4 deep and indicated only by indentation; the OSA branch calls another policy; and cosmetic purpose / 'documenting evaluation' require judgment.
